title: Dyspareunia
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, hot flashes, night sweats, mood changes, and irregular menses/amenorrhea. FSH is elevated (>40), estradiol is low. Menopause = 12 months of amenorrhea. Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (atrophic vaginitis): thinning and drying of vaginal mucosa from estrogen loss → dyspareunia, pruritus, increased UTIs. Treatment: for vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes) — systemic HRT (estrogen ± progestin) for shortest duration at lowest dose. Contraindications: breast cancer, VTE, stroke. For GU symptoms only — vaginal estrogen (cream, ring, tablet). Non-hormonal: lubricants, moisturizers, SSRIs/SNRIs for hot flashes. Osteoporosis prevention: calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, screening DEXA.

stacks.label: Vaginal estrogen (cream/ring/tablet)
stacks.finding: For GU symptoms. Minimal systemic absorption.
